newsitem.title: USA: U.S. condemns retribution over land sales to Jews.
newsitem.headline: U.S. condemns retribution over land sales to Jews.

text.p: The United States on Thursday urged Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to maintain the rule of law in his territory and said it would condemn any official backing for retribution against Arabs selling land to Jews.

The State Department comments came after an Israeli court ordered the detention of a Palestinian man and woman on suspicion of involvement in the murder of an Arab alleged by Israel to have been killed for selling land to Jews.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns condemned the killing as "a savage murder" and said "the people who committed that murder ought to be brought to justice."

"If it turns out that there was any kind of official sanction given to encourage people to go after Arabs who are selling land, then, obviously, the United States would condemn in the strongest possible terms any kind of extrajudicial action that would affect innocent Palestinians," he said.

"We think it's very important that Chairman Arafat and the Palestinian Authority officials involved emphasise that the rule of law must apply in territories controlled by the Palestinian Authority," Burns told a news briefing.

Washington had told the Palestinians that "there can be no place for public threats against civilians or anyone else in the Middle East at this time," and wanted to see a public condemnation of such threats, he added.

Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Meddein was quoted in a published report 12 days ago as saying that Palestinians who sold land to Jews faced execution. Last week, the body of 70-year-old Farid Bashiti was found in the West Bank town of Ramallah.
But Burns said the United States understood that a recent Palestinian Authority decree on land sales did not specifically invoke the death penalty for those selling land to Jews.
"There is no comment or reference in the decree ... to the death penalty ... and the decree does not specify whether or not sales of land can be made to Israelis or to Jews," he said.

Burns condemned what he called "some vitriolic public statements" on the issue, but also quoted Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat as saying the death penalty in such cases was not Palestinian policy.
"It would be good to see a reaffirmation of that," he said.
